newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba driving carefully due to weak mark - Jochimsen.
newsitem.headline: Buba driving carefully due to weak mark - Jochimsen.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen, referring to the bank's decision to hold open the option of reviewing its main money market rate in two weeks' time, said on Friday that this showed the Bundesbank was driving carefully in the current environment.

In comments made to the Handelsblatt newspaper and published in Friday's edition, Jochimsen said: "Normally we stress that we do not follow an exchange rate-oriented policy. Now we want to make people aware that we are driving carefully, making sure we can see the road clearly."
The Bundesbank's policy-making council began its four-week summer break on Thursday after setting its main money market rate, the repo, in advance for just two of the four weeks.

In the past, during phases when it has been regularly setting the repo rate at a fixed level in its council meetings, the central bank has usually also announced its intentions for the whole of the holiday period in advance.
Analysts interpreted yesterday's move as signalling that the central bank was keeping its options open in case of any turbulence on financial markets.

But Jochimsen added in his comments that the decision by no means signalled that the Bundesbank would automatically switch to a variable rate repo tender -- where banks bid for rates -- with a view to allowing rates to edge slightly higher.
"For the moment the issue for the Bundesbank was to set a signal," the article said, paraphrasing Jochimsen's words.
He also said there had been no discussion about plans for concerted intervention at the meeting, a according to the newspaper.
